source: A fern made of smaller ferns
videos.handover: The first activity opens: grow the Sierpinski Carpet one step at a time.
videos.note: The chapter opener: a fern made of smaller ferns, left open.

source: Draw Steps 0, 1 and 2 of the Sierpinski Carpet and count the

items.question: Draw Steps 0, 1 and 2 of the Sierpinski Carpet and count the remaining squares and the holes at each step.
steps: Step 0: one whole square, no hole.
Step 1: a 3 by 3 grid with the centre removed leaves 8 squares and 1 hole.
Step 2: each of the 8 squares loses its own centre, so 8 × 8 = 64 squares remain.
Holes at Step 2: the old hole plus 8 new ones, 1 + 8 = 9.
items.answer: Remaining squares 1, 8, 64; holes 0, 1, 9

videos.answer: Remaining squares 1, 8, 64; holes 0, 1, 9

source: Find the number of remaining squares at Step 3 and at Step 4

items.question: Find the number of remaining squares at Step 3 and at Step 4 of the Sierpinski Carpet.
steps: Step 2 has 8 × 8 = 64 remaining squares.
Step 3: each of these gives 8, so 64 × 8 = 512.
items.answer: 512 squares at Step 3 and 4096 at Step 4

videos.answer: 512 squares at Step 3 and 4096 at Step 4

source: Find the number of holes at Step 3 and at Step 4 of the Sier

items.question: Find the number of holes at Step 3 and at Step 4 of the Sierpinski Carpet.
steps: Holes at Step 3: 1 + 8 + 64 = 73.
Step 3 has 512 remaining squares, and each makes a new hole at Step 4.
Holes at Step 4: 73 + 512 = 585.
items.answer: 73 holes at Step 3 and 585 at Step 4

videos.answer: 73 holes at Step 3 and 585 at Step 4

source: An equilateral triangle has side 8 cm. Show that joining the

items.question: An equilateral triangle has side 8 cm. Show that joining the midpoints of its sides makes 4 identical equilateral triangles.
steps: Each corner triangle has two sides of 8 ÷ 2 = 4 cm with the 60° angle of the big triangle between them.
It is isosceles, so its base angles are equal: (180° − 60°) ÷ 2 = 60° each.
All its angles are 60°, so it is equilateral and its third side is also 4 cm.
The middle triangle has the three third sides as its sides: 4 cm, 4 cm and 4 cm.
items.answer: Four equilateral triangles, each of side 4 cm

videos.answer: Four equilateral triangles, each of side 4 cm

source: For the Sierpinski Triangle with starting area 1 square unit

items.question: For the Sierpinski Triangle with starting area 1 square unit, find the remaining triangles, the holes and the remaining area at Step 3.
steps: Remaining triangles: 3 × 3 × 3 = 27.
Area: each step keeps 3 of 4 parts, so 3/4 × 3/4 × 3/4 = 27/64 square unit.
items.answer: 27 triangles, 13 holes and 27/64 square unit of area

videos.answer: 27 triangles, 13 holes and 27/64 square unit of area

source: Figure it Out (sierpinski fractals, question 1)

items.question: Draw the initial few steps (at least till Step 2) of the shape sequence that leads to the Sierpinski Triangle.
steps: Step 0: draw an equilateral triangle.
Step 1: join the midpoints of its sides and shade out the middle triangle; 3 triangles remain.
Step 2: repeat on each of the 3 corner triangles; 3 × 3 = 9 triangles remain.
items.answer: Step 0 is one triangle, Step 1 shows 3 triangles around 1 hole, Step 2 shows 9 triangles and 4 holes

videos.answer: Step 0 is one triangle, Step 1 shows 3 triangles around 1 hole, Step 2 shows 9 triangles and 4 holes

source: Figure it Out (sierpinski fractals, question 2)

items.question: Find the number of holes, and the triangles that remain at each step of the shape sequence that leads to the Sierpinski Triangle.
steps: Each remaining triangle gives 3 remaining triangles at the next step: 1, 3, 9, 27, so the count at Step n is 3 to the power n.
Each remaining triangle also makes one new hole, and the old holes stay.
At Step n the holes are 1 + 3 + 9 + ... up to 3 to the power (n − 1), which equals (3 to the power n, minus 1) divided by 2.
items.answer: Remaining triangles: 3 to the power n. Holes: 1 + 3 + 9 + ... up to n terms, which is (3 to the power n, minus 1) divided by 2

videos.answer: Remaining triangles: 3 to the power n. Holes: 1 + 3 + 9 + ... up to n terms, which is (3 to the power n, minus 1) divided by 2

source: Figure it Out (sierpinski fractals, question 3)

items.question: Find the area of the region remaining at the nth step in each of the shape sequences that lead to the Sierpinski fractals. Take the area of the starting square/triangle to be 1 sq. unit.
steps: Carpet: each step keeps 8 of the 9 equal parts of every square, so the area is multiplied by 8/9.
After Step 2 the carpet has 8/9 × 8/9 = 64/81 square unit left.
Triangle: each step keeps 3 of the 4 equal parts, so the area is multiplied by 3/4.
After Step 2 the triangle has 3/4 × 3/4 = 9/16 square unit left.
items.answer: Carpet: (8/9) to the power n square unit. Triangle: (3/4) to the power n square unit. Both shrink towards 0

videos.answer: Carpet: (8/9) to the power n square unit. Triangle: (3/4) to the power n square unit. Both shrink towards 0

source: Start with an equilateral triangle of side 1 unit. Find the

items.question: Start with an equilateral triangle of side 1 unit. Find the number of sides, the length of each side and the perimeter at Step 1 of the Koch Snowflake.
steps: Each side is cut into 3 parts of 1/3 unit, and the middle part is replaced by two sides of a bump.
So each side becomes 4 sides: 3 × 4 = 12 sides.
Each side is 1/3 unit long.
Perimeter = 12 × 1/3 = 4 units.
items.answer: 12 sides, each 1/3 unit, perimeter 4 units

videos.answer: 12 sides, each 1/3 unit, perimeter 4 units

source: A diamond pattern has area 64 square cm. Each new shape is d

items.question: A diamond pattern has area 64 square cm. Each new shape is drawn by joining the midpoints of the sides of the one before. What is the area of the third shape inside?
steps: Joining the midpoints keeps exactly half the area each time.
First shape inside: 64 ÷ 2 = 32 square cm.
Second: 32 ÷ 2 = 16 square cm.
Third: 16 ÷ 2 = 8 square cm.
items.answer: 8 square cm

videos.answer: 8 square cm

source: Figure it Out (koch snowflake, question 1)

items.question: Draw the initial few steps (at least till Step 2) of the shape sequence that leads to the Koch Snowflake.
steps: Step 0: draw an equilateral triangle with sides of 9 units on dot paper so thirds are easy.
Step 1: on each side raise a bump on the middle third; a six pointed star with 12 sides appears.
Step 2: put a smaller bump on the middle third of each of the 12 sides.
items.answer: Step 0 has 3 sides, Step 1 is a star with 12 sides, Step 2 has 48 sides

videos.answer: Step 0 has 3 sides, Step 1 is a star with 12 sides, Step 2 has 48 sides

source: Figure it Out (koch snowflake, question 2)

items.question: Find the number of sides in the nth step of the shape sequence that leads to the Koch Snowflake.
steps: Step 0 has 3 sides.
Each step turns every side into 4 sides, so the count is multiplied by 4.
items.answer: 3 × (4 to the power n) sides at Step n

videos.answer: 3 × (4 to the power n) sides at Step n

source: Figure it Out (koch snowflake, question 3)

items.question: Find the perimeter of the shape at the nth step of the sequence. Take the starting equilateral triangle to have a sidelength of 1 unit.
steps: At Step n there are 3 × (4 to the power n) sides.
Each step makes every side one third as long, so each side is 1/3 to the power n.
Each step multiplies the perimeter by 4/3.
items.answer: 3 × (4/3) to the power n units; the perimeter keeps growing

videos.answer: 3 × (4/3) to the power n units; the perimeter keeps growing

source: A square has side 4 cm. Its corners are cut off from midpoin

items.question: A square has side 4 cm. Its corners are cut off from midpoint to midpoint. Find the area of the square that is left and of the square made from the four corners.
steps: The starting square has area 4 × 4 = 16 square cm.
Each corner triangle has two sides of 2 cm at a right angle: area 2 × 2 ÷ 2 = 2 square cm.
The four corners together: 4 × 2 = 8 square cm, and they fit together into a square.
The square left over: 16 − 8 = 8 square cm.
items.answer: Both squares have area 8 square cm, half of the starting square

videos.answer: Both squares have area 8 square cm, half of the starting square

source: Cut the corners at the thirds of an equilateral triangle of

items.question: Cut the corners at the thirds of an equilateral triangle of side 9 cm and of a square of side 9 cm. Find the side lengths of the shapes left.
steps: Triangle: each side keeps its middle third of 9 ÷ 3 = 3 cm.
Each cut corner is an equilateral triangle of side 3 cm, so each cut edge is 3 cm: a regular hexagon of side 3 cm.
Square: each side keeps its middle third of 3 cm.
Each cut edge is the slanted side of a right triangle with sides 3 cm and 3 cm: √(3² + 3²) = √18, about 4.24 cm.
So the octagon has sides 3 cm and about 4.24 cm, and it is not regular.
items.answer: A regular hexagon of side 3 cm; an octagon with sides 3 cm and about 4.24 cm, not regular

videos.answer: A regular hexagon of side 3 cm; an octagon with sides 3 cm and about 4.24 cm, not regular

source: A tin can is a cylinder with radius 3 cm and height 10 cm. W

items.question: A tin can is a cylinder with radius 3 cm and height 10 cm. What profile does it show from directly above, and what from the side?
steps: From directly above you see the round lid: a circle of radius 3 cm.
From the side you see the height and the width: a rectangle.
The width of the rectangle is the diameter, 2 × 3 = 6 cm, and its height is 10 cm.
items.answer: A circle of radius 3 cm from above; a 6 cm by 10 cm rectangle from the side

videos.answer: A circle of radius 3 cm from above; a 6 cm by 10 cm rectangle from the side

source: Give two different solids that each show a rectangular profi

items.question: Give two different solids that each show a rectangular profile from one viewpoint and a triangular profile from another.
steps: A tent shaped triangular prism: from the front a triangle, from the side a rectangle.
A square pyramid seen from the side gives a triangle, but from above it gives a square, which is a rectangle with equal sides.
So both a triangular prism and a square pyramid work, and there are more.
items.answer: A triangular prism and a square pyramid, among others

videos.answer: A triangular prism and a square pyramid, among others

source: A cylinder has radius 7 cm and height 14 cm. Picture it befo

items.question: A cylinder has radius 7 cm and height 14 cm. Picture it before you draw it: what profile does it show from the side, and what from directly above?
steps: From the side you see its width and its height.
The width is the diameter: 2 × 7 = 14 cm, and the height is 14 cm.
Width and height are equal, so the side profile is a square of side 14 cm.
From directly above you see the round top: a circle of radius 7 cm.
items.answer: A square of side 14 cm from the side and a circle of radius 7 cm from above

videos.answer: A square of side 14 cm from the side and a circle of radius 7 cm from above

source: Count the faces, edges and vertices of a triangular prism.

items.question: Count the faces, edges and vertices of a triangular prism.
steps: Faces: 2 triangles and 3 rectangles, so 2 + 3 = 5.
Edges: 3 on each triangle and 3 joining them, so 3 + 3 + 3 = 9.
Vertices: 3 on each triangle, so 3 + 3 = 6.
items.answer: 5 faces, 9 edges, 6 vertices

videos.answer: 5 faces, 9 edges, 6 vertices

source: A prism has two congruent 10 sided polygons as opposite face

items.question: A prism has two congruent 10 sided polygons as opposite faces. Find its faces, edges and vertices.
steps: Faces: 10 parallelograms and 2 polygons, 10 + 2 = 12.
Vertices: 10 + 10 = 20.
items.answer: 12 faces, 30 edges, 20 vertices; for n sides, n + 2 faces, 3n edges and 2n vertices

videos.answer: 12 faces, 30 edges, 20 vertices; for n sides, n + 2 faces, 3n edges and 2n vertices

source: A pyramid has a 10 sided base. Find its faces, edges and ver

items.question: A pyramid has a 10 sided base. Find its faces, edges and vertices.
steps: Faces: 10 triangles and the base, 10 + 1 = 11.
Vertices: 10 + 1 = 11.
items.answer: 11 faces, 20 edges, 11 vertices; for n sides, n + 1 faces, 2n edges and n + 1 vertices

videos.answer: 11 faces, 20 edges, 11 vertices; for n sides, n + 1 faces, 2n edges and n + 1 vertices

source: A gift box is a prism on an octagon, and its lid is a pyrami

items.question: A gift box is a prism on an octagon, and its lid is a pyramid on the same octagon. Find the faces, edges and vertices of each.
steps: Prism, n = 8: faces 8 + 2 = 10, edges 3 × 8 = 24, vertices 2 × 8 = 16.
Pyramid, n = 8: faces 8 + 1 = 9, edges 2 × 8 = 16, vertices 8 + 1 = 9.
Check the prism: faces + vertices − edges = 10 + 16 − 24 = 2.
Check the pyramid: 9 + 9 − 16 = 2.
items.answer: Octagonal prism: 10 faces, 24 edges, 16 vertices; octagonal pyramid: 9 faces, 16 edges, 9 vertices

videos.answer: Octagonal prism: 10 faces, 24 edges, 16 vertices; octagonal pyramid: 9 faces, 16 edges, 9 vertices

source: A cross shaped net has a column of four squares A, B, C, D f

items.question: A cross shaped net has a column of four squares A, B, C, D from top to bottom, and two squares L and R on either side of B. Fold it into a cube with B as the bottom. Which faces are opposite each other?
steps: B is the bottom; A, C, L and R fold up as the four walls.
D is attached to C, so it folds over the top: D is opposite B.
A and C are on opposite sides of B, so they are opposite walls.
L and R are on opposite sides of B, so they are opposite walls too.
items.answer: B and D, A and C, L and R are the pairs of opposite faces

videos.answer: B and D, A and C, L and R are the pairs of opposite faces

source: Six squares: a row of four, one square above the first squar

items.question: Six squares: a row of four, one square above the first square of the row, and one more square to the left of that square. Is it a net of a cube?
steps: The row of four folds round into four walls; call the first square the front.
The square above the front folds over as the lid.
The last square is attached to the left edge of the lid, so it folds down onto the left wall.
Two faces land on the left wall and the bottom is missing.
items.answer: No, it is not a net of a cube

videos.answer: No, it is not a net of a cube

source: Draw a net of a cuboid 4 cm by 2 cm by 1 cm and find the are

items.question: Draw a net of a cuboid 4 cm by 2 cm by 1 cm and find the area of the net.
steps: Rectangles needed: two of 4 cm by 2 cm, two of 4 cm by 1 cm, two of 2 cm by 1 cm.
Draw the walls in a row: 4 by 1, 2 by 1, 4 by 1, 2 by 1, all 1 cm tall.
Attach two 4 by 2 rectangles above and below a 4 by 1 wall as the top and bottom.
Area = 2 × (8 + 4 + 2) = 28 square cm.
items.answer: A net of six rectangles with area 28 square cm

videos.answer: A net of six rectangles with area 28 square cm

source: Figure it Out (nets, question 1)

items.question: Which of the following are the nets of a cube? First, try to answer by visualisation. Then, you may use cutouts and try. (i) two squares on top and a row of four below, joined only at the second square; (ii) a row of three on top and a row of three below, joined at one square; (iii) a staircase of 2, 2 and 2 squares; (iv) a row of four with one square above and one below the third square; (v) a row of four with two squares hanging in a column below the second square; (vi) a row of four with one square above the third square and one below the second square.
steps: (i): the row of four makes the walls, one square becomes the lid, and the sixth square folds onto a wall: not a net.
(ii): the 3 and 3 staircase folds with no overlap: a net.
(iii): the 2, 2, 2 staircase folds with no overlap: a net.
(iv) and (vi): a row of four with one square above and one below: nets.
(v): both extra squares are below the row, so one lands on a wall: not a net.
items.answer: (ii), (iii), (iv) and (vi) are nets of a cube; (i) and (v) are not

videos.answer: (ii), (iii), (iv) and (vi) are nets of a cube; (i) and (v) are not

source: Figure it Out (nets, question 2)

items.question: A cube has 11 possible net structures in total. In this count, two nets are considered the same if one can be obtained from the other by a rotation or a flip. Find all the 11 nets of a cube.
steps: Row of four with one square above and one below: 6 nets (the extra squares above positions 1 to 4 and below positions 1 to 4, removing turns and flips).
Row of three in the middle: 3 nets with 1 square on one side and 2 on the other, and 1 net of two rows of three.
The staircase of 2, 2 and 2: 1 net.
items.answer: 6 nets with a row of four, 4 with a longest row of three, and 1 staircase: 11 in all

videos.answer: 6 nets with a row of four, 4 with a longest row of three, and 1 staircase: 11 in all

source: Figure it Out (nets, question 3)

items.question: Draw a net of a cuboid having sidelengths: (i) 5 cm, 3 cm, and 1 cm (ii) 6 cm, 3 cm, and 2 cm
steps: (i): two rectangles 5 by 3, two 5 by 1, two 3 by 1; walls in a row 5, 3, 5, 3 long and 1 cm tall, with 5 by 3 rectangles above and below a 5 cm wall.
Area of net (i) = 2 × (15 + 5 + 3) = 46 square cm.
(ii): two rectangles 6 by 3, two 6 by 2, two 3 by 2; walls 6, 3, 6, 3 long and 2 cm tall, with 6 by 3 rectangles above and below a 6 cm wall.
Area of net (ii) = 2 × (18 + 12 + 6) = 72 square cm.
items.answer: Nets of six rectangles in three equal pairs, with areas 46 square cm and 72 square cm

videos.answer: Nets of six rectangles in three equal pairs, with areas 46 square cm and 72 square cm

source: Four shapes are made of equilateral triangles: a large trian

items.question: Four shapes are made of equilateral triangles: a large triangle of 4, four triangles that all meet at one point, a straight strip of 4, and a strip of 4 with a fifth triangle below. Which are nets of a regular tetrahedron?
steps: A regular tetrahedron has 4 faces with 3 meeting at each corner.
The large triangle of 4 folds its three corners up to meet: a net.
Four triangles around one point would put 4 faces at one corner: not a net.
The straight strip of 4 folds into a tetrahedron: a net.
The last shape has 5 triangles, one too many: not a net.
items.answer: Only the large triangle and the straight strip of 4

videos.answer: Only the large triangle and the straight strip of 4

source: A cylinder has radius 7 cm and height 10 cm. Find the sides

items.question: A cylinder has radius 7 cm and height 10 cm. Find the sides of the rectangle in its net, using π as 22/7.
steps: The long side wraps once round the base: the circumference 2 × π × 7.
The short side is the height, 10 cm.
items.answer: A 44 cm by 10 cm rectangle with two circles of radius 7 cm

videos.answer: A 44 cm by 10 cm rectangle with two circles of radius 7 cm

source: A cone has base radius 5 cm and slant length 10 cm. What fra

items.question: A cone has base radius 5 cm and slant length 10 cm. What fraction of a full circle of radius 10 cm is its unrolled curved surface?
steps: The arc of the sector equals the base circumference: 2 × π × 5 = 10π cm.
A full circle of radius 10 cm has circumference 2 × π × 10 = 20π cm.
Fraction = 10π ÷ 20π = 1/2.
items.answer: Half of the circle: a semicircle of radius 10 cm

videos.answer: Half of the circle: a semicircle of radius 10 cm

source: An octahedron is two square pyramids joined at their square

items.question: An octahedron is two square pyramids joined at their square bases. Plan a net for it with equilateral triangles, and count its faces, edges and vertices.
steps: Each pyramid gives 4 triangles around its apex, so the octahedron has 4 + 4 = 8 faces.
Unfold the top 4 triangles as a fan around the top corner, and the bottom 4 as a fan around the bottom corner.
Join the two fans along one edge of the square, one fan on each side of it: 8 triangles with no overlap.
Edges: 4 round the square, 4 up to the top and 4 down to the bottom, so 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.
Vertices: 4 on the square, the top and the bottom, so 4 + 1 + 1 = 6.
items.answer: Two fans of 4 equilateral triangles joined along one edge; 8 faces, 12 edges and 6 vertices

videos.answer: Two fans of 4 equilateral triangles joined along one edge; 8 faces, 12 edges and 6 vertices

source: A cube has side 4 cm. An ant is at the centre of a side face

items.question: A cube has side 4 cm. An ant is at the centre of a side face and a laddu at the centre of the top face. Find the length of the shortest path.
steps: Unfold the top face so it sits flat above the side face.
The ant is 2 cm below the shared edge and the laddu is 2 cm beyond it, on the same straight line.
Shortest path = 2 + 2 = 4 cm.
items.answer: 4 cm, straight up the middle of the side face and across to the centre of the top

videos.answer: 4 cm, straight up the middle of the side face and across to the centre of the top

source: A cube has side 6 cm. An ant is at the centre of the front f

items.question: A cube has side 6 cm. An ant is at the centre of the front face, and a laddu at the middle of the edge between the top face and the right face. Find the shortest path.
steps: Unfold the right face so it lies flat beside the front face.
From the ant, the laddu is now 3 + 3 = 6 cm across and 3 cm up.
Shortest path = √(6² + 3²) = √45, about 6.71 cm.
Going up 3 cm and then across 6 cm would be 9 cm, which is longer.
items.answer: About 6.71 cm, a slanted straight line on the net

videos.answer: About 6.71 cm, a slanted straight line on the net

source: A cuboid is 8 cm by 4 cm by 4 cm. An ant is at the centre of

items.question: A cuboid is 8 cm by 4 cm by 4 cm. An ant is at the centre of a 4 cm by 4 cm end face. A laddu sits on a long bottom edge, 2 cm from that end. Find the shortest path.
steps: Unfold the end face flat against the long face that meets the laddu's edge.
On this net the ant is 2 cm into the end face and 2 cm from the bottom edge line.
The laddu is 2 cm on the other side of the fold, on the bottom edge line.
So the line goes 2 + 2 = 4 cm along and 2 cm across.
Shortest path = √(4² + 2²) = √20, about 4.47 cm.
items.answer: About 4.47 cm

videos.answer: About 4.47 cm

source: For the 30 cm by 12 cm by 12 cm box, compare the 42 cm route

items.question: For the 30 cm by 12 cm by 12 cm box, compare the 42 cm route with the slanted unfolding whose right triangle has sides 24 cm and 32 cm.
steps: Straight route: 11 + 30 + 1 = 42 cm.
Slanted route: d² = 24² + 32² = 576 + 1024 = 1600.
40 cm is less than 42 cm.
items.answer: The slanted route of 40 cm is shorter than 42 cm

videos.answer: The slanted route of 40 cm is shorter than 42 cm

source: A stick 5 cm long is held above a table so that one end is 3

items.question: A stick 5 cm long is held above a table so that one end is 3 cm higher than the other. How long is its projection on the table?
steps: The stick, its projection and the height difference make a right triangle.
The stick is the longest side, 5 cm; the height difference is 3 cm.
Projection = √(5² − 3²) = √16 = 4 cm.
items.answer: 4 cm, shorter than the stick

videos.answer: 4 cm, shorter than the stick

source: A square card of side 5 cm is tilted about one of its sides

items.question: A square card of side 5 cm is tilted about one of its sides so that the opposite side is 3 cm higher. What is its projection on the floor?
steps: The two sides parallel to the floor keep their length of 5 cm.
Each of the other two sides is 5 cm long and rises 3 cm, so it projects to √(5² − 3²) = 4 cm.
Parallel sides stay parallel, and the angles at the hinge stay right angles.
items.answer: A rectangle 5 cm by 4 cm

videos.answer: A rectangle 5 cm by 4 cm

source: A cone standing on its base has base radius 4 cm. Name three

items.question: A cone standing on its base has base radius 4 cm. Name three different solids whose projection on the floor is the same circle.
steps: The cone's projection on the floor is a circle of radius 4 cm.
A cylinder standing upright with radius 4 cm gives the same circle.
A ball of radius 4 cm and a bowl with rim radius 4 cm give it too.
items.answer: A cylinder, a ball and a bowl, each with radius 4 cm

videos.answer: A cylinder, a ball and a bowl, each with radius 4 cm

source: A rod 13 cm long is held above a table so that one end is 5

items.question: A rod 13 cm long is held above a table so that one end is 5 cm higher than the other. Predict the length of its projection, and say when the projection would be 13 cm.
steps: The rod, its projection and the height difference make a right triangle with the rod as the longest side.
The projection equals 13 cm only when the rod is held parallel to the table.
items.answer: 12 cm; it would be 13 cm only with the rod parallel to the table

videos.answer: 12 cm; it would be 13 cm only with the rod parallel to the table

source: A cylinder of radius 3 cm and height 8 cm stands on its base

items.question: A cylinder of radius 3 cm and height 8 cm stands on its base. Draw its front, top and side views.
steps: Front view: the width is the diameter 2 × 3 = 6 cm and the height is 8 cm, a rectangle.
Top view: the round top, a circle of radius 3 cm.
Side view: the same as the front, a 6 cm by 8 cm rectangle.
items.answer: Front and side views are 6 cm by 8 cm rectangles; the top view is a circle of radius 3 cm

videos.answer: Front and side views are 6 cm by 8 cm rectangles; the top view is a circle of radius 3 cm

source: Four identical cubes: three in a row on the floor, and one m

items.question: Four identical cubes: three in a row on the floor, and one more on top of the left cube. Draw its front, top and side views.
steps: Front view: 3 squares in a row with 1 square on top of the left one, an L of 4 squares.
Top view: looking down, the top cube covers the cube under it, so 3 squares in a row.
Side view: looking from the left, the row is hidden behind one cube, so a column of 2 squares.
items.answer: Front: an L of 4 squares; top: a row of 3 squares; side: a column of 2 squares

videos.answer: Front: an L of 4 squares; top: a row of 3 squares; side: a column of 2 squares

source: Figure it Out (views of solids, question 1)

items.question: Observe the front view, top view and side view of the different lines in Fig. 4.6. Is there any relation between their lengths?
steps: Each view is a projection, so no view is longer than the line itself.
A view shows the full length only when the line is parallel to that plane.
If a line goes a cm along, b cm deep and c cm up, the views have squared lengths a² + c², a² + b² and b² + c².
Adding these gives twice a² + b² + c², which is twice the square of the line's length.
items.answer: No view is longer than the line; the squares of the three view lengths add up to twice the square of the line's length

videos.answer: No view is longer than the line; the squares of the three view lengths add up to twice the square of the line's length

source: Figure it Out (views of solids, question 2)

items.question: Find the front view, top view and side view of each of the following solids, fixing its orientation with respect to the vertical, horizontal and side planes: cube, cuboid, parallelepiped, cylinder, cone, prism, and pyramid.
steps: Cube on a face: three squares.
Cuboid on a face: three rectangles.
Parallelepiped leaning forward: a parallelogram from the side, rectangles from the front and top.
Cylinder standing: rectangle, circle, rectangle.
Cone standing: triangle from the front and side, a circle with its centre point from the top.
Triangular prism with its triangle facing front: a triangle from the front, rectangles from the top and side.
Square pyramid standing: triangles from the front and side, a square with both diagonals from the top.
items.answer: Cube: squares; cuboid: rectangles; cylinder: rectangle, circle, rectangle; cone: triangle, circle, triangle; prism: triangle and rectangles; pyramid: triangles and a square with diagonals

videos.answer: Cube: squares; cuboid: rectangles; cylinder: rectangle, circle, rectangle; cone: triangle, circle, triangle; prism: triangle and rectangles; pyramid: triangles and a square with diagonals

items.question: A toy 10 cm tall stands 50 cm in front of a wall. A torch shines straight at the wall from 50 cm in front of the toy. How tall is the shadow? What if the torch is moved to 150 cm in front of the toy?
steps: The rays spread from the torch, so the shadow and the toy make similar triangles.
Torch to wall is 50 + 50 = 100 cm, twice the torch to toy distance.
With the torch at 150 cm, torch to wall is 150 + 50 = 200 cm.
Shadow = 10 × 200 ÷ 150 ≈ 13.3 cm, closer to the toy's 10 cm.
items.answer: 20 cm, then about 13.3 cm: the farther the torch, the closer the shadow is to the projection

videos.answer: 20 cm, then about 13.3 cm: the farther the torch, the closer the shadow is to the projection

items.question: A square card has diagonals of 10 cm. It is tilted in sunlight about one diagonal, so the other diagonal's shadow is 6 cm. What is the shadow, and how long is each side?
steps: The diagonal on the hinge stays 10 cm; the other diagonal's shadow is 6 cm.
The shadows of the diagonals still cross at right angles at their midpoints, and opposite sides stay parallel.
So the shadow is a rhombus with diagonals 10 cm and 6 cm.
Each side = √(5² + 3²) = √34, about 5.83 cm.
items.answer: A rhombus with sides of about 5.83 cm

videos.answer: A rhombus with sides of about 5.83 cm

items.question: Imagine eight identical cubes, glued together along faces to form the letter C. (i) This looks like a C from the front. What does it look like from the side? From the top? (ii) Glue additional cubes to make a shape that looks like one letter from the front and another from the top. (iii) Now, can you glue even more cubes to make it look like three given letters from the front, top and side? (iv) Can you think of other letter combinations to make with a single combination of cubes in this manner?
steps: The C is 4 cubes tall: a row of 3 on top, 1 cube on the left in each of the two middle rows, and a row of 3 at the bottom, 3 + 1 + 1 + 3 = 8.
From the side every row hides behind its first cube: a column of 4 squares, like the letter I.
From the top the rows stack under each other: a row of 3 squares.
For (ii) to (iv), add cubes behind the front letter so the top view spells the second letter, then check the side view.
items.answer: (i) From the side a column of 4 squares, from the top a row of 3 squares; (ii) to (iv) are built by adding cubes behind the letter

videos.answer: (i) From the side a column of 4 squares, from the top a row of 3 squares; (ii) to (iv) are built by adding cubes behind the letter

source: A glass cube balanced on a corner is projected onto the floo

items.question: A glass cube balanced on a corner is projected onto the floor. How many of its 12 edges form the hexagon outline, and how many lie inside it?
steps: The top and bottom corners both project to the centre of the hexagon.
The 3 edges at the top corner and the 3 at the bottom corner run from the centre outwards: 3 + 3 = 6 inside.
The remaining 12 − 6 = 6 edges form the outline.
All 12 projections have the same length, so the outline is a regular hexagon.
items.answer: 6 edges make the regular hexagon and 6 run inside from its centre

videos.answer: 6 edges make the regular hexagon and 6 run inside from its centre

items.question: Draw a 2 by 2 by 2 cube on an isometric grid. How many units of line do its visible edges use?
steps: A box seen in isometric shows 9 edges: 3 along height, 3 along length, 3 along depth.
Each edge of this cube is 2 units long.
Total = 9 × 2 = 18 units.
items.answer: 18 units of line over 9 visible edges

videos.answer: 18 units of line over 9 visible edges

items.question: Draw a cuboid 1 unit long, 2 units deep and 3 units tall on the grid. How many units of line do its visible edges use?
steps: 3 visible edges along length, each 1 unit: 3 × 1 = 3.
3 visible edges along depth, each 2 units: 3 × 2 = 6.
3 visible edges along height, each 3 units: 3 × 3 = 9.
Total = 3 + 6 + 9 = 18 units.
items.answer: 18 units of line

videos.answer: 18 units of line

items.question: In addition to the 5 ways shown in Fig. 4.8, are there any additional ways of gluing four cubes together along faces? Can you visualise and draw these as well?
steps: The 5 tetris shapes all lie flat.
Lift one cube out of the flat plane: an L of three cubes with a fourth cube on top of the corner cube gives the tripod, three arms meeting at a corner.
An S shape with one end lifted up gives a twisted screw, and its mirror image twists the other way.
So there are 3 more, 5 + 3 = 8 in all.
items.answer: Yes: 3 more, the tripod and two mirror image screws, for 8 ways in all

items.question: Observe this triangle. (i) Would it be possible to build a model out of actual cubes? What are the front, top, and side profiles of this impossible triangle? (ii) Recreate this on an isometric grid. (iii) Why does the illusion work?
steps: (i) No: each corner looks like a right angle bend, but three such bends cannot close into a triangle in real space. A real model of rows of cubes looks right only from one viewpoint.
(ii) Draw each arm as a row of cubes along a grid direction and join the ends where they appear to meet.
(iii) An isometric drawing loses depth: a near end and a far end can project to the same point, so the eye joins them.
items.answer: It cannot be built; the illusion works because the projection loses depth, so far and near ends appear to touch
